heading: Alpha node
text:
### Alpha node [IRET.6.1]

An alpha node represents one pattern-schema participation
in the network. It holds:

- A reference to the schema it matches.
- A list of inline alpha tests (constraints that can be
  checked on the fact alone, without joining against
  other patterns).
- An alpha memory: the set of facts currently satisfying
  this node's tests.
- A list of downstream beta inputs to notify on
  memory changes.

`ds_rete_alpha_node_t` is declared in `runtime/src/libds/rete/alpha.h`.

idris.name: Iret_6_1__alpha
idris.note: One pattern-schema participation: the schema, its inline tests over one fact [IRET.6.2] as a predicate, and its memory. The downstream-input list is not stored: a beta node references its alpha [IRET.6.6], so dispatch walks the chains instead. Expression evaluation is out of scope; a test is a Bool predicate.

idris.name: Iret_19__view
idris.note: THE VIEW of an engine: working memory distinct; every alpha memory distinct and equal to its schema's facts passing its tests in working-memory order; every chain consistent from the nil token. Kept by every operation below.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_5__recomputed
idris.note: What the view says of an engine: every alpha memory is its schema's admitted facts, and every terminal holds exactly its chain's recompute over working memory, without duplicates.

idris.name: Iret_6_1__same_alphas
idris.note: Two alpha lists of one shape: at every index the same schema and tests; the memories may differ.

idris.name: iret_6_1__same_alphas_refl
idris.note: An alpha list has its own shape.
